issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Exposed to Others: I feel that others can see what happened to me just by looking at me
issues.explanation: The negative appraisal items 'others can see what happened to me' and 'ashamed of what happened to my body' imply a trauma with visible bodily violation or injury, most classically interpersonal/sexual trauma, and are hard to reconcile with a generic man-made disaster trauma in the absence of any corroborating memory or trigger content about bodily injury or disfigurement.

issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Body Shame: I feel ashamed of what happened to my body
issues.explanation: 'Avoid Being Touched' is specifically linked to bodily violation/contact-based trauma and fits poorly with the rest of the profile for man-made disaster. The threat items center on environmental danger and escape planning, creating a cross-node mismatch with this touch-avoidance strategy.

issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Body Shame: I feel ashamed of what happened to my body
issues.explanation: These items imply a trauma with prominent bodily violation or physical injury consequences. For a man-made disaster trauma, this specific body-focused pattern is not impossible, but in the absence of any supporting memory or trigger content and alongside the other items emphasizing generalized danger, it stands out as a hard-to-explain shift toward an assault/injury formulation.

issues.item: Maladaptive Strategies: Avoid Being Touched: Any form of physical contact with others
issues.explanation: Within the current profile, avoidance of touch and bodily stress appears organized around bodily harm/shame, but the threat items are about environmental danger, escape planning, and unfamiliar places. That makes the strategy set only partially connected to the expressed threat/appraisal pattern.

issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Failed Role: I have failed in my most important role in life
issues.explanation: The profile is otherwise centered on persistent danger, vigilance, scanning, escape planning, and avoidance of unfamiliar places, which coheres with threat-focused beliefs after a man-made disaster. 'Failed Role' introduces a distinct self-evaluative theme that is not supported by the rest of the selected items and is hard to reconcile with this otherwise purely danger/safety formulation. Given the active formulation emphasizes Negative Appraisals → Maladaptive Strategies and Maladaptive Strategies → Threat, a danger-based appraisal would better fit the linked hypervigilance and checking strategies than a role-failure appraisal.

vignette: Sunita, a 32-year-old South Asian woman and single city council member, has been grappling with intense anxiety since she survived a chemical spill at her office building two years ago. The event left her feeling vulnerable and constantly on edge about potential threats. The incident was sudden and terrifying. Sunita remembers the choking fumes and the chaos as people rushed to evacuate. She felt overwhelmed by the sheer unpredictability of it all, and since then, she has come to believe that the world is a dangerous place where anything can happen without warning. This belief has driven her to adopt several maladaptive strategies to cope with her constant fear. What frightened her most was the realization that she could not control or predict such events. Consequently, Sunita began avoiding situations that put her body under stress, like exercising or engaging in any physical exertion. She also became hyper-vigilant towards people around her, constantly scanning for signs of danger and identifying escape routes wherever she goes. These behaviors have become so ingrained that she feels an overwhelming sense of relief only when she can avoid unfamiliar places where the level of danger remains unknown. Sunita's fear has deepened over time as she became increasingly aware of her heightened vulnerability at night, when it is harder for her to feel safe. She began planning escape routes in every new environment she enters, a behavior that stems from her constant vigilance and belief that she needs to be especially careful because you never know what can happen next. Her occupation has been significantly impacted by these behaviors. As a city council member, Sunita often attends late-night meetings or public gatherings where the risk of another disaster feels disproportionately high. She finds herself constantly scanning her surroundings for any signs of danger and avoiding physical stress during long hours of standing or walking through crowded streets after events. Sunita's friends have noticed changes in her behavior as well. She has become more isolated, declining invitations to social gatherings and unfamiliar venues where she cannot assess the level of threat. This has strained many of her relationships, leaving her feeling increasingly alone and misunderstood. The cycle has tightened over time. Her constant vigilance makes it harder for her to trust that any place is truly safe, reinforcing her negative appraisals about the world being dangerous. These beliefs then lead her to adopt more maladaptive strategies, which in turn increase her perceived threat levels. She finds herself caught in a loop where each layer of fear and avoidance only serves to heighten her overall sense of vulnerability. What finally brought Sunita to seek help was a recent incident at work where she had a panic attack during an important meeting due to the physical stress of standing for long hours. This event made her realize that her fears were increasingly interfering with her ability to perform her duties and maintain personal relationships. She is now seeking therapy, hoping to regain control over her life and reduce her pervasive sense of danger. Sunita's journey has been marked by a deep-seated belief in the world's inherent danger and an intense need for constant vigilance. Her maladaptive strategies have become so deeply embedded that they exacerbate her fear and avoidance, making it increasingly difficult to function without the looming threat of another disaster.
